currency.mpRateNote: Monetary Policy Rate cut 250bps to 10.75% at the 30 September 2026 MPC (from 13.25%), the lowest in several years, as inflation eased back inside the BoZ target band. trendAnalysis.direction: USD/ZMW market mid at 20.1503 (2.02% weaker vs the 9 Oct snapshot at 19.7508). The kwacha eased across the whole basket on the latest open.er-api.com print (updated 12 Oct), with the BoZ official mid last published at 19.75 (6 Oct).

Policy continuity after the 1 Sep 2026 inauguration of President Hichilema and Vice-President for a second term

trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha weakened broadly in the latest session, with the USD/ZMW market mid at ~K20.1503 (open.er-api.com, 12 Oct) versus ~K19.7508 in the prior snapshot - a +2.02% move (more kwacha per dollar). The softening ran across the whole basket: GBP (26.688, +2.22%), EUR (22.5917, +2.06%), ZAR (1.2211, +2.73%), BWP (1.4557, +3.29%) and CNY (3.0139, +2.47%) all cost more kwacha. This marks a break above the 18.40-19.80 band the pair had held through late September/early October. The policy backdrop remains the 30 September 2026 MPC, at which the BoZ cut the MPR 250bps to 10.75% - the lowest in several years - as inflation (6.1% y/y in September, per ZamStats) returned inside the 6-8% target band; that trims the carry support that buoyed the kwacha earlier in 2026. Import demand, copper-price swings, the pace of further BoZ easing and the 9 October opening of the 14th National Assembly (2026/2027 policy direction) are the near-term reference points.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 19.20–20.50 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.50–20.50 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
